title: Basic English — Course 2, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 10

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. Which containers are for clean plastic bottles?
tasks.audioText: The college is changing the labels on its recycling bins from next week. Paper and cardboard should go into the blue containers, while clean plastic bottles should be placed in the yellow containers. Food waste must not be put into either bin. The student environment team will visit classrooms on Monday to explain the new system and answer questions.
options: The blue containers
The yellow containers
The green containers
The grey containers

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. What will the student environment team do on Monday?
tasks.audioText: The college is changing the labels on its recycling bins from next week. Paper and cardboard should go into the blue containers, while clean plastic bottles should be placed in the yellow containers. Food waste must not be put into either bin. The student environment team will visit classrooms on Monday to explain the new system and answer questions.
options: Visit classrooms to explain the system and answer questions
Inspect recycling bins and record contamination
Change the collection schedule
Publish the new bin labels on the college website

tasks.prompt: A college recycling trial produced mixed results because students were unsure which materials belonged in each bin. The environment team observed the bins and found that many items were placed in the wrong container. They introduced clearer labels with examples and moved the bins closer to the places where waste was produced. The next review will compare contamination levels before and after the changes. Reading 1. Why did the trial produce mixed results?
options: The bins were too far from the classrooms
Students were unsure which materials belonged in each bin
The signs did not explain how to sort plastic
The collection service arrived at the wrong time

tasks.prompt: What will the next review compare?
options: The total weight of waste collected each week
The number of bins installed around the college
The total amount of plastic collected over the year
Contamination levels before and after the changes
will be introduced
introduce yesterday
will introducing
are introduce

tasks.prompt: Choose TWO ways to make a recycling system easier to use.
options: Use identical labels for every container
Mix all materials together
Use clear labels with examples
Place bins where waste is produced

tasks.prompt: The unwanted material mixed into a recycling container is called ___.
A student is unsure which bin to use. What is the most helpful response?
options: Put it anywhere; it does not matter.
Ignore the question and leave the item on the floor.
Let's check the label together and find the correct container.
Use the nearest bin without checking.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of recycling systems in a logical order.
options: Label each container clearly
Identify the types of waste produced
Review contamination and improve the system
Choose suitable containers
correctOrder: Identify the types of waste produced
Review contamination and improve the system

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words suggesting how your college could improve recycling. Explain one problem, two changes and how success could be checked.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: one recycling problem is identified (0–2); two practical changes and a way to check whether they work are described (0–2); the proposal is logically linked with understandable grammar (0–2); recycling/waste vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are appropriate (0–2).
